results.title: Mid-Region Metropolitan Planning Organization Open Data Site Content
results.description:
Use this group to organize the items that you want to share as part of your site. Shared items become available in your site's search results and only people who have access to these items will be able to find them. Members of the core team get access to shared items and can update them at any time. Certain cards, like the Gallery card, will automatically populate with shared items so that you don't have to search for them when choosing what you want to display on your site.

Contact support with any questions related to this group or content management for your site.

DO NOT DELETE THIS GROUP.

results.title: Climate Change Hazards Vulnerability Assessment Tool
results.snippet: Mapping tool for assessing climate equity and prioritizing hazard mitigation interventions in the Albuquerque Metro Planning Area based on tract-level demographic indicators of where populations of concern for health vulnerability and environmental justice consideration are residentially concentrated within areas of relatively heightened risk for exposure to natural hazards such as extreme heat, wildfire and flooding.
results.accessInformation: Raster tree canopy inventory created by Steven Bassett of the Nature Conservancy for the MRCOG regional planning area using Google Earth Engine analysis of 2020 NAIP imagery. Land Surface Temperature data layer was produced by GIS staff of the Pima Association of Governments upon request in Fall 2021 using a data model developed by Senior GIS Analyst Benjamin Hickson.

results.title: MRCOG Planning for Equity Communities Viewer
results.description:
Data Sources:

*Please refer to the original data source for data verification and grant eligibility requirements.
This map is for reference purposes only.

Disadvantaged Communities of The Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ)'s 

  • Climate & Economic Justice Screening Tool
  • Transportation Disadvantaged Census Tracts of the USDOT mapping tool

  • Areas of Persistent Poverty & Historically Disadvantaged Communities 
    of the USDOT     Grant Project Location Verification mapping tool. 

  • The American Communities Survey of the U.S. Census Bureau

For more information, please see the following links:

Justice40 Initiative | Environmental Justice | The White House

The RAISE grant program and Area of Persistent Poverty definitions:

https://www.transportation.gov/RAISEgrants/raise-areas-persistent-poverty
https://datahub.transportation.gov/stories/s/tsyd-k6ij

US Department of Transportation
Federal Tools to Determine Disadvantaged Community Status | US Department of Transportation

Instructions:

  • Click on the layers button to see all available layers and turn on/off visibility
  • Click on any census tract to see a pop-up with further details
  • If you're unsure of which tract to check, try the address search bar in the upper left corner
  • To review this information at any time, click the "i" information icon in the upper left

Problems viewing the map? Please contact gis@mrcog-nm.gov.
results.snippet: This mapping application was prepared by the Metropolitan Planning Organization of the Mid-Region Council of Governments in New Mexico for member governments and community organizations to collect demographic data resources from various Federal sources* identifying "Areas of Persistent Poverty", "Historically Disadvantaged Communities", and others named as priority recipients of the RAISE grant and other federal funding opportunities of the Justice40 Initiative. It can also be used to identify areas where vulnerable populations and those of concern for environmental justice are concentrated within the region to inform hazard mitigation and equity planning initiatives.

results.title: Natural Resource Inventory- Web App
results.snippet: Test web app of the Natural Resource Inventory, using the Web App format instead of the dashboard format. Testing compatability between applications and map viewers.

results.title: Air Quality and Health Equity
results.snippet: Map series presenting data on six air pollutant measures of the EPA's 2021 release of the Environmental Justice Screen 2.0 tool in relation to the MRMPO Vulnerability Index census tract demographics indicating relative concentrations of populations of concern for environmental justice - persons with incomes below poverty, persons of color, and of Hispanic/Latine ethnic origins.  Additional demographic measures of populations of concern for health vulnerability taken from the Social Vulnerability Index of the CDC (such as children, seniors, and persons with disabilities) are also included in pop-up windows by clicking on individual tracts within the map.  The tool is provided to assist in performance of environmental justice assessments of disproportionate environmental health impacts, and inform actions to support improved and equitable health outcomes.

results.title: MRCOG Roadway Safety and Crash Report (2015-2019)
results.description:
This story map visualizes emerging crash trends in the MRCOG region through a tabbed story map consisting of maps, dashboards, and charts. Data visualized includes crash types by year, mode, and top contributing factor.

This story map is intended to visualize and to help analyze crash trends to develop targeted safety interventions.
results.licenseInfo:
Data sources:
MRMPO Roadway Transportation Safety Action Plan (RTSAP)
MRCOG's Environmental Justice (EJ) Index
MRCOG's High Fatality & Injury Network (HFIN)
NMDOT Traffic and Safety Bureau

results.title: HFIN 2017-2021 Story Map
results.description:
The High Fatal & Injury Network (HFIN)  

The HFIN was developed to help target funding to the most dangerous streets and intersections and get the biggest bang for our "safety buck".   

The HFIN symbolizes segments with high levels of fatal and injury crashes per mile, and fatal and injury intersection crash rates (divided by approaching traffic) for every major road (arterials and collectors) in the region.   

The HFIN score is derived from summing the number of fatal and injury crashes on every link and then dividing that number by the length of the link in miles. The number of fatal crashes on each link is multiplied by 2 to give them greater significance than injury crashes.  

The formula for the HFIN Score for any given link is: (fatal crashes *2) + injury crashes/ length of link in miles.  

The HFIN links that have an HFIN Score of 319.8 or higher (2 times the regional mean or higher) make up only 2.5% of the major roadway network. However, 26% of the fatalities and 40% of the injury crashes happened on these roadways between 2017 and 2021.  

The HFIN links that have an HFIN score of 159.9 or higher (simply above the regional mean) make up only 8% of the major roadways, but contain 47% of the fatal crashes and 64% of the injury crashes. 

Interstates were not included because they are maintained and operated by the NMDOT. For more about NMDOT safety initiatives check out their Planning Division.

results.title: How do crashes impact vulnerable communities? StoryMap
results.description:
Crashes tend to happen at higher rates in communities that have high concentrations of poverty and people of color. Historically, these are the same communities that have been underrepresented in the planning process. Because these neighborhoods bear a disproportionate share of negative societal impacts, they are often referred to as “vulnerable communities”. The Metropolitan Transportation Plan identifies these communities in terms of a regional Environmental Justice (EJ) index.  

See the map below showing fatal crashes with MRCOG's Environmental Justice (EJ) Index. The EJ Index combines the percentage of households living in poverty with the percentage of persons of color in a census tract to create an "EJ score" between 2 and 10. The higher the score, the more vulnerable the community, represented by darker shades in the map below.
